clue.text: Fit a jacket around exhibits in the Louvre

indicators.note: the jacket is wrapped around the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a tux, short for tuxedo, is a dinner jacket
fit as in capable means able

explanation.surface: A tailor fits a jacket on a visitor admiring the exhibits in the Louvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a verb about tailoring, but it means capable; the jacket is split around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux are pictures or staged scenes, and the French plural suits works shown in a Paris gallery.

clue.text: Aircraft with missile aimed at it — it ends up in the sea

definitions.text: it ends up in the sea

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
SAM is a surface-to-air missile

explanation.surface: A plane is shot at by a missile and crashes into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard, which finishes up floating in or sunk under the sea.

clue.text: Odd penny coin once given to pork pie purveyor

parts.note: the ecu was an old French coin, and later a European unit of account
pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie, so a purveyor of them is a liar

explanation.surface: Someone hands an old penny over to a butcher selling pork pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' is British rhyming slang for 'lie' (a pork pie is a meat pastry), so the 'purveyor' is not a butcher but a teller of lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar and odd are synonyms, both meaning strange or unusual.

clue.text: Plant supplying a drink in South Africa

indicators.note: the drink sits inside the country code

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A shrub from which a local beverage is brewed in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Slippery character in Longfellow's "Last Stand"

indicators.note: only the final letter of the poet's name is wanted

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A shifty figure appears in a poem by Longfellow called Last Stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress 'Last Stand' as a title; in fact 'last' picks W from Longfellow's and 'Stand' is EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a slippery, untrustworthy person, from the animal's sly reputation.

clue.text: Was first to keep song inexpressive

indicators.note: the first piece holds the song inside it

parts.note: to come first in a race is to have won
an ode is a lyric poem or song

explanation.surface: A singer led the field by keeping to a song without any expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden performance is stiff and lacking in expression.

clue.text: Bloke's last "Letter From America" comes back in German

definitions.note: read as 'bloke is', a man plus the link

indicators.note: the turned letters go inside the German abbreviation

parts.note: the last letter of the alphabet as Americans say it is zee

explanation.surface: A man's final broadcast of the radio talk Letter From America is replayed in German.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter From America was Alistair Cooke's long-running BBC radio talk; here it means how Americans name the alphabet's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Geezer is British slang for a man, a synonym of bloke.

clue.text: Undo docking and sell on?

definitions.meaning: docking is cutting off an animal's tail, so to undo it is to put a tail back on
to sell goods to the public is to sell them on after buying wholesale

explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking' suggests ships, but here it is the clipping of tails; read the answer as RE-TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is selling goods to the public; re-tail would be giving back a lost tail.

clue.text: Want source kept quiet

indicators.note: the source holds the quiet letter within it

parts.note: a word's derivation is its source
P (piano) means quiet in music

explanation.surface: A journalist's informant was kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Deprivation is a lack or want of necessities, the noun sense of want.

clue.text: Author of "The Bird Who Broke the Professor's Heart"

parts.note: a fowl is a bird

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A novel's title, The Bird Who Broke the Professor's Heart, names its author.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title is invented; 'Who Broke the' only links. The heart of Professor's (ignoring the apostrophe) is ES.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fowles was an English novelist, author of The French Lieutenant's Woman.

clue.text: Oriental toffs with a lack of social distinction

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
the quality is an old term for the upper classes, the toffs

explanation.surface: Eastern aristocrats who nevertheless believe in a classless society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toffs' is British slang for posh upper-class people, once collectively called 'the quality'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality means no difference in rank, so it is an absence of social distinction.

clue.text: Given direction by a bird lover

parts.note: to be led is to be given direction

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is guided to the right place by an enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus came to Leda as a swan, so she is the lover of a bird, not a birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Leda was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan, making her a bird's lover.

clue.text: Notes girl receiving drink on a plate

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
gin is a drink
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A girl is handed a drink on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: MARIA splits as MAR...IA around GIN, A and L; L for learner plate is a British driving convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalia are notes scribbled in the margins of a book.

clue.text: Naturally produced a maiden over?

parts.note: over in the sense of surplus, an extra
a maiden is a virgin

explanation.surface: A bowler naturally produced a maiden over in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over is a cricket over with no runs scored; here 'maiden' is VIRGIN and 'over' is EXTRA. Extra virgin olive oil is cold-pressed without chemical refining.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra-virgin oil comes from the first pressing without heat or chemicals, so made in a natural way.

clue.text: It regulates the power that makes toaster hot

indicators.note: the pieces are made into something new, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A thermostat-like device controls the power that heats a toaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control electric current.

clue.text: Poor soldier brought up in middle of Depression

indicators.note: the turned soldier goes inside the hollow

parts.note: an indent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are lifted, so read upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A penniless soldier is raised during the Great Depression.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'brought up' means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy or impoverished, a synonym for poor.

clue.text: Unproductive river running dry

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
supplies that are running dry are low

explanation.surface: A river that is drying up yields nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallow land is left unplanted, so it produces nothing for a season.

clue.text: Good drummer required for "An American in Puerto Rico"?

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer

explanation.surface: A fine drummer is wanted for a show called An American in Puerto Rico.
explanation.definitionFit: Gringo is a Latin American term for a foreigner, especially a North American.

clue.text: Freedom fighter's infiltrated trade towers, literarily

indicators.note: the revolutionary gets inside the trade word

parts.note: to barter is to trade
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A guerrilla has sneaked into skyscrapers in a centre of commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: Barchester Towers is a novel by Anthony Trollope, hence 'literarily'; 'towers' is not tall buildings but part of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel title pairs the fictional cathedral town with Towers, so that word in literature calls it up.

clue.text: Metal providing Switzerland with capital

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A metal that brings Switzerland money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium, a metallic element, or the shiny plating made from it.

clue.text: Tease aristocrat about tape

parts.note: to rib is to tease

indicators.note: about in the sense of turned about, facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nob is a toff or aristocrat

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a lord over a strip of tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon is a narrow strip of material, much like a tape.

clue.text: Stitch up with a euphemistic oath

definitions.meaning: to mend a hole with stitches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' tempts as slang for framing someone, but here it means sewing a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Darning is mending with stitches; darn is also a softened curse.

clue.text: Lots of booze turned humble character inside out

indicators.note: the turned peasant goes within the cut booze
most of the word is kept, with its tail cut

parts.note: booze is alcohol

indicators.note: turned in the sense of facing the opposite way, so the word's letters run backwards

parts.note: a serf is a lowly peasant

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker who used to be a humble man has been completely transformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' reads as one phrase, but 'out' alone is the definition; 'Lots of' cuts the tail off the booze word.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, outdoors, so out rather than in.

clue.text: Ford's history, say, swallowed by Scottish fool

indicators.note: the example goes inside the other word

parts.note: Henry Ford said history is bunk
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A Scottish idiot believes Henry Ford's verdict on the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford, the carmaker, famously said 'History is more or less bunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Begunk is a Scots verb meaning to trick or make a fool of someone.

clue.text: Credit cut back for digger

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: running a tab is buying on credit
to mow is to cut grass

explanation.surface: A bank's credit is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TAB and MOW together, giving WOM then BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is an Australian marsupial that digs burrows.

clue.text: Tolerated nothing on the island

parts.note: borne means put up with, tolerated
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone put up with having nothing on the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in Southeast Asia, shared by three countries.
